author: Coconino News
title: City announces temporary road closures as part of repair program
text:
Becky Daggett, Mayor | City of Flagstaff
Becky Daggett, Mayor | City of Flagstaff
As part of the City of Flagstaff's annual Road Repair and Street Safety (RRSS) program, northbound Beulah Blvd will be closed at Forest Meadows St on Monday, July 21 for pavement patching. This work is in preparation for a full pavement overlay scheduled in August. The closure will last less than 24 hours, and southbound traffic on Beulah Blvd will remain unaffected.
Additional work is scheduled under the RRSS program throughout the community. Temporary lane shifts, lane closures, or shoulder closures are expected on several roadways during specific timeframes:
- Kaspar Dr & Lynch Ave: July 21 – July 25 - concrete forming and placement
- Beulah Blvd: July 21 – pavement patching
- Switzer Canyon Dr: July 22 – pavement patching
- San Francisco St: July 23 & 24 – pavement patching
- Timberline Rd: July 25 – pavement patching
The City and its contractor are working to minimize the impact of this work on local residents and businesses. The annual Road Repair and Street Safety program is funded by Flagstaff voters’ approval of Proposition 406 in 2014, which established a $100 million, 20-year dedicated sales tax for road repair and street safety projects.
For more information or project updates, visit flagstaff.az.gov/roadrepair. Questions related to this project can be directed to City of Flagstaff Senior Project Manager Jarrett Nelson at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection).
